recipes.name: Quesabirria
recipes.description: A modern fusion of traditional Mexican birria stew and quesadillas, born in Tijuana, known for its rich, fat-stained tortillas and accompanying dipping broth.
instructions: Slow-braise the meat in a chile-infused broth until tender.
Dip the tortillas into the rendered surface fat of the broth and place on a hot plancha.
Add shredded cheese and meat, fold in half, and griddle until crisp.
Serve with the consommé for dipping.

recipes.name: Cochinita Pibil
recipes.description: A pre-Columbian Yucatan specialty relying on the acidic tenderization of pork and earthy annatto seed, historically roasted in a pib (earth oven).
instructions: Blend the achiote paste with bitter orange juice.
Marinate the pork, then wrap it entirely in layers of banana leaves to retain moisture.
Slow-roast until the meat shreds effortlessly.
Serve with pickled red onions.

recipes.name: Chilaquiles
recipes.description: An ingenious utilization of stale tortillas, transitioning them into a hearty, high-calorie breakfast staple drenched in vibrant salsas.
ingredients: 2 cups salsa roja or salsa verde
instructions: Cut the tortillas into triangles and deep fry until crisp.
Simmer briefly in hot salsa until softened but retaining a slight bite.
Plate and garnish heavily with crema, crumbled cheese, and fried eggs.

recipes.name: Street Cart Elote
recipes.description: The quintessential Mexican street food, transforming roasted corn into a rich, acidic, and spicy vehicle for dairy and chili powder.
ingredients: 4 ears fresh corn on the cob
instructions: Grill the corn until heavily charred and tender.
Slather generously with a mixture of mayonnaise and crema.
Dredge the cob in crumbled cotija cheese and dust thoroughly with chili powder and lime juice.

recipes.name: Camarones al Mojo de Ajo
recipes.description: A coastal dish focusing on the emulsification of massive amounts of garlic into butter and olive oil to gently poach fresh seafood.
instructions: Finely mince the garlic and simmer gently in a heavy emulsion of butter and olive oil until sweet and highly fragrant.
Add the shrimp, searing briefly on high heat until just opaque.
Finish with lime.

recipes.name: Sopa de Lima
recipes.description: A Yucatan soup where the specific bittersweet local lime is the primary aromatic driver, rather than serving as a mere afterthought or garnish.
instructions: Simmer robust chicken broth with roasted tomatoes and whole habanero peppers.
Finish the broth with a heavy dose of fresh Yucatan lime juice.
Serve immediately over crispy fried tortilla strips.

recipes.name: Michoacán Carnitas
recipes.description: A Michoacán specialty where pork is confited in its own rendered lard, yielding incredibly tender meat with shattered, crispy exterior edges.
instructions: Submerge large chunks of pork completely in liquid lard.
Simmer for hours with the aromatics, citrus, and milk to aid caramelization.
Increase the heat at the very end to crisp the exterior of the meat.

recipes.name: Enchiladas Suizas
recipes.description: A mid-century Mexico City invention representing 'Swiss' style due to its heavy dairy component, a departure from pre-Hispanic culinary norms.
instructions: Lightly fry the tortillas to make them pliable, then roll with chicken.
Blend roasted tomatillos with crema to form a rich salsa verde.
Blanket the rolls in the sauce and cheese, then bake until bubbling.

recipes.name: Sopa Tarasca
recipes.description: A deeply flavored, pureed bean and tomato soup originating from Michoacán, utilizing dried chiles to create a robust, smoky backbone.
instructions: Blend the cooked pinto beans, roasted tomatoes, and soaked ancho chiles into a completely smooth puree.
Simmer the puree with chicken broth and epazote.
Garnish with crema and crisp tortilla strips.

recipes.name: Aguachile
recipes.description: A Sinaloan seafood dish where raw shrimp is 'cooked' aggressively and rapidly in highly acidic, fiercely spicy lime juice, retaining a snappy texture.
instructions: Butterfly the shrimp.
Blend the lime juice with cilantro and chiles to create a vibrant green liquid.
Submerge the shrimp in the fiery liquid for no more than 15 minutes.
Serve with sliced cucumber and onion.

recipes.name: Queso Fundido
recipes.description: A communal appetizer that relies heavily on the unique melting and stretching qualities of specific Northern Mexican cheeses, paired with spiced meats.
instructions: Crumble and fry the chorizo until crispy.
Melt a thick layer of cheese in a shallow cast-iron skillet under a broiler until bubbling and slightly charred.
Top with the cooked chorizo and rajas, serving immediately with tortillas.

recipes.name: Tlayuda
recipes.description: An Oaxacan icon featuring an oversized, leathery corn tortilla toasted over coals, acting as an edible platter for regional ingredients.
instructions: Smear the large tortilla with asiento and beans.
Toast directly over a charcoal grill until crisp.
Top with shredded Oaxaca cheese, shredded cabbage, and thin cuts of grilled beef (tasajo).

recipes.name: Carlota de Limón
recipes.description: An immensely popular, highly accessible icebox cake that requires absolutely no baking and utilizes shelf-stable dairy introduced during industrialization.
instructions: Vigorously whisk or blend the milks with fresh lime juice until the acid causes the dairy to thicken rapidly.
Layer the cream alternately with Maria cookies in a glass dish.
Freeze until fully set.
